solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exposed area where Spooner's gone bankrupt on unemployment benefit

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words that follow

parts.note: a firm that has gone bankrupt has gone bust
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bleak, exposed place where people have gone broke and live on benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of BUST DOLE gives something said like 'dust bowl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bowl is a drought-stricken region stripped of topsoil, an exposed and barren area.

clue.text: Nodding donkey's initial scraps, oily at the bottom

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here of donkey's

parts.note: scraps as in quarrels or fights are rows

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter, taken from oily

explanation.surface: An oil pump, a nodding donkey, is described with scrap metal and grease at its base.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nodding donkey' is an oilfield pumpjack, which makes the surface seem industrial; 'Nodding' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nodding off is sleepy, their head dropping as they doze.

clue.text: Sexy girl's shown up in place of swine

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed name goes inside the pig pen

parts.note: a sty is where pigs are kept

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the name is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Mae is a girl's name; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A provocative girl is exposed for her behaviour in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sexy girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Sexy' alone defines; 'shown up' (a down reversal) turns the name, and the girl's 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is a common informal synonym for erotic or sexually charged.

clue.text: It's light, when a hunk gets up

indicators.note: in a down clue, gets up means the phrase rises, reading backwards

parts.note: a hunk or chunk of something is a slab

explanation.surface: A well-built man rising in the morning is said to be a light presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' reverses A SLAB to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a famously lightweight wood used for models, so it is light material.

clue.text: Runt, perhaps, scoffing last of corn, in tears

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so the pig takes in a letter

parts.note: a runt is the smallest of a litter of piglets, an example of a wee pig

indicators.note: last of signals the final letter of corn

explanation.surface: The smallest piglet is crying as it gobbles the last of the corn.
explanation.walkthrough: N (from 'last of corn') goes inside WEE PIG; 'wee' is Scottish and informal British for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weeping is crying, which is being in tears.

clue.text: One out of position, very young setter perhaps, gets promotion

indicators.note: out of tells us one letter leaves the word for position

parts.note: a site is a position or location
one is the Roman numeral I
a setter is a dog breed, and a very young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: A player out of position, a baby crossword setter, perhaps, nonetheless wins advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link. 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler; here it is the dog. SITE without I leaves STE.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-up is a rise to a higher level or rank, a promotion.

clue.text: Happen to be a sprinter, knackered

indicators.note: knackered is British slang for worn out, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: It happens that a sprinter is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire means to occur or come about.

clue.text: Fop wants to drop by with bird

parts.note: to drop by someone's house is to pop in
a jay is a bird

explanation.surface: A dandy wants to visit with his bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, conceited dandy, a fop.

clue.text: Girl entering home has first to erect fence

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the name goes inside the home

parts.note: pad is slang for home
Lisa is a girl's name

indicators.note: first to signals the first letter of erect

explanation.surface: A girl going into her house has to put up a fence first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes forming a barrier.

clue.text: Solver that is off, is on

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong signals the letters being rearranged

parts.note: that is abbreviates to i.e., giving IE

explanation.surface: A solver who is off form still claims to be on.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLVER plus IE is rearranged ('off') to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie over something is to rest on top of it, so overlying is being on it.

clue.text: Mini mate, perhaps, producing bone

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British car, an example of the word
a mate or friend is a pal

explanation.surface: A friend in a Mini makes something called bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Mini as an example of a car; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpal is one of the small bones of the wrist.

clue.text: Error which may be shown up

indicators.note: in a down entry shown up means read from the bottom, and this word reads the same that way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A mistake that might come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: A palindrome: written upwards in the grid it is unchanged, so it can be shown up without harm. There is also a cheeky hint at the slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Nice use of topic, as I'm rambling

indicators.note: rambling speech wanders about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for rambling on in a pleasant use of their topic.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPIC, AS and IM are rearranged ('rambling'); 'use of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico means likeable and congenial, a pleasant person, which is nice.

clue.text: Massive fireball is thrown over, causing hole in the head

indicators.note: thrown over means turned the other way, so both words read backwards

parts.note: the sun is a massive ball of burning gas
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge fireball is hurled, leaving a hole in someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown over' reverses SUN IS; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an air-filled cavity in the bones of the skull, literally a hole in the head.

clue.text: Sell game for a return

indicators.note: a return means coming back, so the game's name is read backwards

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.surface: Someone sells off a game in exchange for a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a return' reads GOLF backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is British slang for to sell, often cheaply or pushily.

clue.text: Performer wrapping desperate man in writhing parcel

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the rearranged letters go round the name
writhing means twisting about, so the letters of parcel are mixed up

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strong-man character from the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A man in desperation is wrapped up in a squirming package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' rearranges parcel into LAPCER, which goes round the name; 'in' is a link. Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip strongman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dancer is an entertainer who dances close to a seated client, a kind of performer.

clue.text: Ship with criminal

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
with means and, together with

explanation.surface: A ship carrying a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or outlaw, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Brillo! One's easy!

definitions.meaning: Brillo is a brand of scouring pad, something used to scour pans
one who is easy, offensive British slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a dated, derogatory British slang term.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrubber is both a scouring pad and crude British slang for a woman thought promiscuous.

clue.text: Film the rotter, creating suspicion

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on a window
rust is what rots metal, so it is a rotter

explanation.surface: A movie about a scoundrel makes people suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie and 'rotter' like a cad; 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is a lack of trust, the same as suspicion or doubt.

clue.text: Happy stonemason?

definitions.meaning: a stonemason chips at stone, so is one who chips; the question mark marks the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is informal for cheerful, and literally one who chips, like a stonemason.

clue.text: Rock music?

definitions.meaning: rock as in a ridge of rock near the sea surface
A 1990s British rock band, so their name is a music act; the question mark marks the stretch

explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock in the sea, and Reef was a British rock band.

clue.text: Cook pours liquid over back

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pouring liquid over something wets it

explanation.surface: A cook pours liquid over someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses WETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to cook slowly in liquid.

clue.text: Marine creature, one mounting — another?

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
one is the Roman numeral I
mounting something is being on it

explanation.surface: A sea animal climbs on top of another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine creature' looks like the definition but builds SEAL; 'another?' is the definition, another marine creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lion is a large eared seal, so it is a further marine creature.

clue.text: Lip on end of server, item of crockery

parts.note: lip means cheek or impudence, which is sauce

indicators.note: end of signals the final letter of server

explanation.surface: A waiter chips the rim of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lip' looks like a dish's rim; here it is cheek, SAUCE; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small dish placed under a cup, a piece of crockery.

clue.text: Stand for Monet under top of tobacco plant

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the stand comes below the first letter
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, here of tobacco

parts.note: a painter like Monet works at an easel, a stand

explanation.surface: Monet's stand sits below a tobacco plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Monet was a French painter, hence an easel.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasel is a prickly plant whose heads were used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Extremist stuck in awful traffic

indicators.note: stuck in shows the word lies within the run of letters awful traffic

explanation.surface: A radical is caught in a dreadful jam.
explanation.walkthrough: Look across the join of 'awful traffic'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, an extremist.

clue.text: Expand complex

definitions.meaning: to expand on an idea is to develop it in more detail

explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as a verb means develop in detail, and as an adjective means intricate.

clue.text: Cockney's leather compound

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop their h, so a letter is lost

parts.note: oxhide is leather made from an ox's skin

explanation.surface: A Londoner's leather is turned into a compound.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the East London dialect, known for dropping h sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen and another element.

clue.text: Meal that's right to feed group

indicators.note: to feed means to put into, so the letter goes inside the group

parts.note: a bunch is a group

explanation.surface: A meal that's right for feeding a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Something sweet, it's missing in man's flower

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened sweet goes inside the man's word

parts.note: a man's thing is his

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letters are removed

parts.note: a biscuit is a sweet snack
it, with the 's a link

explanation.surface: A sweet treat lost from a man's flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something sweet, it's missing' reads as a lament, but 'missing' is the removal signal and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibiscus is a shrub with large showy blossoms, a flower.

clue.text: Step down, or go upstairs?

definitions.meaning: to step down is to leave a job
going upstairs at night means going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: To retire is both to stop working and to go to bed.

clue.text: Triangle irregular, though whole

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A triangle that is irregular but still whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means complete in itself, entire or whole.
